messages:
maria: Heads-up — we got a DSAR for a guest account that was used in our demo corpus. Request asks for all personal data and deletion of any derived artifacts (embeddings, indexes). Can privacy ops confirm scope?

alex: Noted. The embeddings live in private-vector-store-prod, encrypted with a customer-managed key (cmk-demo-embeds). We also have daily snapshots in s3://redwood-backups/embeds/ that are versioned. :thinking_face:

jamal: I can take point for the DSAR. Two immediate questions: 1) Are there any snapshots older than TTL that would keep the data? 2) Will rotating the CMK break our ability to delete or re-encrypt existing objects?

maria: Good q. There are ~3 snapshots referencing those embeddings from Jan/Feb that live beyond the 90d TTL because of a pending retention exception for audits. We need to know if we can scrub indexes *and* remove snapshot copies.

kevin: From infra: rotating a KMS key (creating a new primary) doesn't automatically re-encrypt existing S3 objects. Our envelope keys reference the key id in metadata. If we rotate, older objects still reference the previous key version; schedule-key-deletion would fail if data still needs to be accessed.

lia: Legal: if the DSAR requires deletion and there is a conflicting legal hold, we need the hold documented before refusing deletion. Is this DSAR under any current investigation?

jamal: Not that I know of. I checked case #438 and nothing. We should assume no legal hold unless someone flags it.

maria: Action plan proposal: 1) Run targeted delete of embeddings from vector DB and indexes. 2) For backups/snapshots, we request a retention exception removal for the three snapshots and then permanently delete. 3) Coordinate with KMS team to ensure key versions remain available until deletes complete.

alex: Sounds right. Implementation note — vector DB delete is async and uses the service account redwood-privacy-bot. We currently don't have that SA in the `vector-admin` RBAC role in production. I'll need an RBAC grant for a one-hour window.

maria: @kevin can you do a temporary role grant and audit log the change? We need the change reflected in cloudtrail and our internal audit stream.

kevin: I can. Will grant `roles/vector-admin` to service account `redwood-privacy-bot@redwood-prod` for 1 hour via infra-change with justification: "DSAR delete - guest demo embeddings". I'll add a tag to the grant. Will post the policy change id here.

ops-bot: deploybot: role grant request received. Change id: change-99231. Expected roll-out in 3m.

jamal: After deletion, we also need to redact any analytics traces that contain the user identifier. Where do analytics event logs for demo infra live?

alex: They are in es-analytics-prod.solr cluster. Deleting from there requires search-admin role; those logs are also subject to retention exception. Recommend running a scoped delete query: `delete by query: user_email:guest123@example.com AND index:demo_*` and then verify shard compaction.

maria: Can someone confirm KMS key status and whether any rewrap action is needed? If objects reference old key versions and we rotate, we might lose ability to read them to delete.

kevin: Confirmed: cmk-demo-embeds currently has key rotation ON with versions v1..v4. We won't schedule deletion for any key until deletes are complete. No rewrap required. We will mark the key as "do-not-delete" for 48 hours.

lia: Please capture all decisions in the DSAR tracker (link) and include timestamps for role grants and deletes. Legal needs proof of deletion (hashes + audit logs).

jamal: I'll run deletion steps and paste the minimal verification: deleted ids and S3 delete markers. Quick checklist I'll follow:
- Request RBAC grant (change-99231)
- Delete embeddings from private-vector-store-prod
- Delete indexes and run compaction
- Remove S3 snapshots and verify delete markers
- Provide audit logs and S3 object versions list

alex: If helpful, command snippets:
```bash
# list object versions referencing guest id
aws s3api list-object-versions --bucket redwood-backups --prefix embeds/guest123
# delete specific version
aws s3api delete-object --bucket redwood-backups --key embeds/guest123.vec --version-id <version-id>
```

maria: Thank you. Once jamal posts the verification, I'll close DSAR ticket. Two final asks: 1) keep cmk-demo-embeds DO-NOT-DELETE until verification complete, 2) add an audit log entry noting the RBAC grant reason.

kevin: Done — cmk-demo-embeds flagged. Audit log link: https://audit.redwood.internal/changes/change-99231

ops-bot: incidentbot: snapshot-deletion-job started (job-7782).

jamal: Deletion done. Posting minimal proof: 7 embeddings deleted from vector DB ids: [emb-912, emb-913, emb-914, emb-915, emb-916, emb-917, emb-918]. S3 list shows delete markers for versions: v-20240112, v-20240202, v-20240301. Audit logs: https://audit.redwood.internal/logs/438/dsar/entries.json

lia: Received proofs. Legal confirms satisfies DSAR. No legal hold found. Please keep records for 2 years as part of compliance archive.

maria: Closing — RBAC grant revoked (change-99231 revoked), KMS flag removed after 48h. Thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
